Johnson County enrolled 1,112 multiracial students in the 2024-25 school year
Johnson County schools enrolled 1,112 multiracial students in the 2024-25 school year.
Johnson County schools enrolled 1,112 multiracial students in the 2024-25 school year, 1.7% higher than the previous year, according to the Iowa Department of Education.
Johnson County enrolled 18,906 students in the 2024-25 school year. Multiracial students made up 5.9% of the student body, the fourth-largest ethnic group in the county.
Of the county's 40 schools, Iowa City High School reported the largest multiracial enrollment in the 2024-25 school year, with 104 students.
Iowa's certified K-12 enrollment declined slightly in the 2025-26 school year, according to the Iowa Department of Education. Total certified enrollment across public and accredited nonpublic schools fell 0.9% to 515,221 students. Public district and charter school enrollment dropped 1.53% to 473,329 students, while accredited nonpublic school enrollment rose 6.4% to 41,892.
The department also reported that 41,044 students used Students First Education Savings Accounts at accredited nonpublic schools as of the Oct. 1 certified enrollment date.
